messages:
Maya Patel: Heads-up — Nightdash fired a sustained tail-latency alert for the runner path after the 02:00 merge. 99th jumped ~220ms and has been creeping up for 45m.
Jordan Lee: I saw it. SLO breach window around 02:20. Throughput steady, so looks like latency regression not load.
ops-bot: alert: nightdash/runner-tail-latency | rule=99th_latency | value=720ms | baseline=500ms | spike_start=3367888800
Samir Khan: Kicking off the perf-prober against the canary now. Starting with kernel selector traces + batching histograms. Will attach profiles when done.
Anita Gomez: My first-pass suspicion is prefetch/batching slewing — the prefetch heuristic seems to overfetch and evict hot KV entries under certain stride patterns. That would explain tail-only increase.
Lee Chen: I can repro a small-scale variant locally: sequences with alternating short/long prompts cause prefetch to map to the heavy kernel path then time out on KV hits.
Jordan Lee: CI perf job also showing regressions: perf-ci-runner-99 failing on nightly with +12% 99th. ci-bot shows recent green -> red after merge 3367879001 (merge/runner-sweep).
ci-bot: perf-ci-runner-99: FAILED (99th latency +12%) — job: https://ci/internal/builds/9421
Samir Khan: Profile dump (sampled stacks from canary):
```
# top stacks
0x7f2a3ef runner::kernel_selector::score() +0x1a0
0x7f2a3f1 runner::batcher::dispatch() +0x120
0x7f2b402 kv::cache::evict_if_needed() +0x88
0x7f2b410 runner::exec::main_loop() +0x2c4
```
Heap churn +15% and a hot calle has shifted from batching->kernel scoring into kv eviction.
Anita Gomez: That lines up. New selector scoring added a small penalty to cached-kernel path to prefer newer 'fast' kernels; combined with batch coalescing it triggers prefetch for longer sequences and pushes KV working set thrash.
Maya Patel: Can we bisect to the exact commit? I want a short list before we decide rollback.
Jordan Lee: Running git bisect on the canary branch now. Initial hint points at commit 3367879001 -> 3367881004 range.
Samir Khan: Bisect result: culprit=commit 3367880337 (runner: tweak kernel scoring weights). Patch reduces affinity to cached kernels.
Lee Chen: Repro test with the revert patch applied locally drops 99th back to baseline.
Maya Patel: Options: 1) revert scoring tweak (fast), 2) patch selector to respect KV hotness signal (longer), 3) throttle prefetch when eviction temp spike detected (medium). Thoughts?
Anita Gomez: Short-term revert seems safest for tonight. We'll put a follow-up to rework the scoring to read KV hit-rate metric before changing kernel affinity.
Jordan Lee: I'll open a revert PR and create a canary rollback. Also pausing the rollout.
Jordan Lee: PR: https://git/internal/runner/pull/2389 (revert: tweak kernel scoring weights)
ops-bot: deploy: canary rollback initiated by Jordan Lee — job 7942 — status=started
Samir Khan: Leaving traces and full perf profiles in the issue: https://jira/internal/browse/RUNNER-512 — includes perf-prober results + flamegraphs.
Maya Patel: Thanks all. Action items: Jordan=roll back PR + block rollout, Samir=attach full profiles and evictions hist, Anita/Lee=design selector fix that accounts for KV hotness, I'll follow up with PM for release notes.
Lee Chen: Noted. Will add a regression test in perf-suite for alternating short/long prompt pattern.
Maya Patel: Good. Marking nightdash alert as triaged for now, will reopen if spikes resume after rollback. :white_check_mark:
Jordan Lee: +1, monitoring.
ci-bot: perf-ci-runner-99: re-run queued after revert PR.
Maya Patel: Closing thread once CI green.
